messages.subject: Allometric Trajectories Analysis
parts:
Hi there,
I am a new user in this field and facing some issues with some analysis. 

I did an analysis of how the shape changes with different population types before and after allometry correction. But I got comments from one of my reviewers as below: 

"Before correcting for allometry in this manner you need to confirm that your groups share a common allometric trajectory. Essentially this is a test of Coords ~ Size*Type. If the interaction is significant, groups do not share common slopes and instead, you need to compare the different allometric trajectories rather than correcting for common allometry. If that interaction is not significant then you can proceed with allometry correcting as you did."

I ran the following code-
> fullmodsize2 <- procD.lm(dat2$coords ~ Csize*poptype + Csize*poptype/site, data = geodf)
> anova(fullmodsize2)
> plot(fullmodsize2, size = dat2$Csize, logsz = TRUE, type = "regression", reg.type = "PredLine", predictor = log(geodf$Csize), pch = 19, col = as.numeric(geodf$poptype))

                    Df      SS       MS     Rsq       F       Z Pr(>F)  
Csize                1 0.04776 0.047760 0.09325 66.0244  9.2061  0.001 **
poptype              2 0.06324 0.031620 0.12347 43.7119 11.7981  0.001 **
Csize:poptype        2 0.01093 0.005467 0.02135  7.5577  6.9040  0.001 **
Csize:poptype:site  14 0.07343 0.005245 0.14336  7.2505 15.7210  0.001 **
Residuals          438 0.31684 0.000723 0.61858                          
Total              457 0.51220                                          
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

This interaction seems significant, but my question is which interaction gives more appropriate results from the following to test that:
 > fullmodsize2 <- procD.lm(dat2$coords ~ Csize*poptype + Csize*poptype/site, data = geodf                       or,
> fullmodsize1 <- procD.lm(dat2$coords ~ Csize * poptype + poptype/site, data = geodf)  or,
> allo.unique <- procD.lm(dat2$coords ~ Csize * poptype/site, iter = 99, RRPP=TRUE, data = geodf)  or, 
> allo.common <- procD.lm(dat2$coords ~ Csize + poptype/site, iter = 99, RRPP=TRUE, data = geodf)

Later, I compared the different allometric trajectories. First, I looked at how the shape changes at min and max sizes by using shape.predictor as follows-

> preds <- shape.predictor(dat2$coords, x= log(dat2$Csize), Intercept = TRUE, predmin =  min(log(dat2$Csize)), predmax = max(log(dat2$Csize)))
> plotRefToTarget(mshape(dat2$coords), preds$predmin, mag=1.5)
> plotRefToTarget(mshape(dat2$coords), preds$predmax, mag=1.5)

I also compared the allometric trajectories in different size ranges. 
> preds1 <- shape.predictor(dat2$coords, x= log(dat2$Csize), Intercept = TRUE, method = "PLS", pred2 = 2.4, pred3 = 2.2, pred4 = 2.4, pred5 = 2.6, pred6 = 2.8, pred7 = 3.0) 
> plotRefToTarget(mshape(dat2$coords), preds1$pred2, mag=0.5)
> plotRefToTarget(mshape(dat2$coords), preds1$pred3, mag=0.5)
> plotRefToTarget(mshape(dat2$coords), preds1$pred4, mag=0.5)
> plotRefToTarget(mshape(dat2$coords), preds1$pred5, mag=0.5)
> plotRefToTarget(mshape(dat2$coords), preds1$pred6, mag=0.5)
> plotRefToTarget(mshape(dat2$coords), preds1$pred7, mag=0.5)

But is there any way of comparing the shape of a particular size (min and max maybe) for different population types? Above all gives me a grid of common body shape changes. But I want to have three different grid plots for the different population types. 

I also did the pairwise comparisons. Does the below trajectories analysis worth doing? 
> TA <- trajectory.analysis(fullmodesize2, groups = geodf$poptype, traj.pts = geodf$site, pca = TRUE, print.progress = FALSE)
> summary(TA, attribute = "SD")
> TP <- plot(TA, pch = 19, cex = 0.7, col = as.numeric(geodf$poptype))
add.trajectories(TP, traj.bg = 1:nlevels(geodf$poptype), start.bg = 1:nlevels(geodf$poptype),end.bg = 1:nlevels(geodf$poptype))
> summary(TA, attribute = "SD") # SD= Shape differences trajectories
Trajectory analysis
100 permutations.
Points projected onto trajectory PCs
Trajectories:
Trajectories hidden (use show.trajectories = TRUE to view)

Pairwise trajectory shape differences, plus statistics
                                            d UCL (95%)           Z Pr > d
Chatham Coastal:Chatham Landlocked  0.4322844 0.6564523 -0.36006097  0.638
Chatham Coastal:Mainland Coastal    0.5334438 0.8297494 -1.81942906  0.958
Chatham Landlocked:Mainland Coastal 0.6159263 0.7787542 -0.04288519  0.515

Am I on the right track that the reviewers ask for? 

Thanks in advance. 

Kind regards,
Motia

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Allometric Trajectories Analysis
parts:
Motia,

 

Your post had several components, and my response here addresses the main points related directly to the reviewer comments. First, your model of shape ~ Size*Pop finds a significant interaction with a large effect size. This means that the allometric trends across poptypes are not consistent, which then means that allometric ‘correction’ using a common slope is incorrect.

 

What the reviewer then requests is a comparison of slopes. This is done using the function ‘pairwise’ in RRPP: geomorph’s companion package.  If you look at the help file of that function, there is an example of comparing slopes. One fits the full model, uses pairwise, and then summarizes using test.type = “VC” (vector correlations). This is what the reviewer requested.


Your post then asked about what interaction gives a more significant result. That is harder to answer, as there is both a conceptual and a statistical component to the question. My first question would be: what is the most appropriate model to be using given your data, your biological design, etc. That should dictate analytical procedure more than which model is more ‘significant’. To me this seems more ancillary to the reviewer’s question.

 

Hope this helps.

 

Dean
